# ModemLens

> ModemLens is a free, open-source tool (MIT licence) by K-I-Soft that reads a USB cellular modem directly in the browser, over WebUSB or Web Serial in Chrome and Edge. It shows what the modem is, whether it is on the network and how good the signal is. There is no server: modem data stays in the browser.

## What it reads

Model, firmware, SIM state, operator, registration, signal quality (RSRP, RSRQ, SINR, RSSI), serving and neighbouring cells, LTE bands, data connections and USB mode.

## How it works

- The automatic scan sends read commands only and changes nothing on the modem.
- Settings such as APN, USB mode or NAT change only in the Actions tab, one at a time and after confirmation, on the Quectel EC200A, an ASR-based stick and the SIMCom SIM7000.
- Tools in the Actions tab work on any modem that knows their commands: SIM PIN (unlock, change, PIN request on or off), USSD codes, manual network choice, reading, deleting and sending text messages, ping, a speed test, and the data traffic the modem counted, with a live chart of its current speed. Every change asks first.
- The speed test runs only when started. It exchanges test data with Cloudflare's speed test service and asks RIPEstat which network it went through. Nothing read from the modem is sent.
- The shareable report masks identifiers such as IMEI, IMSI and ICCID. A full export needs a confirmation.
- The page sets no cookies and loads no tracking or third-party scripts. Page downloads appear in the server logs, which K-I-Soft evaluates for visitor statistics.

## Which modems work

- Modems that answer AT commands over USB or a serial port. Tested profiles exist for the Quectel EC200A and an ASR-based UFI stick (USB ID 1286:4e3c). Other AT modems get a standard command set.
- Sticks without AT commands are read through a bookmark on the stick's own admin page, or over the stick's own Wi-Fi. Confirmed on the Huawei E3372h HiLink (web page at 192.168.8.1) and the MediaTek UF909 (ZTE-style web page at 192.168.0.1). A Unisoc-based stick that answers neither AT nor a known web page is not supported yet.
- On Windows, USB direct needs the WinUSB driver on the modem's AT interface. With the vendor's driver, use Serial port instead.
- Firefox and Safari do not offer WebUSB or Web Serial, so ModemLens does not work there.

- [Demo with a made-up modem](https://modemlens.k-i-soft.ch/?demo=1): the same interface, no hardware needed
- [Source code](https://github.com/k-i-soft/modemlens): MIT licence
- [K-I-Soft](https://www.k-i-soft.ch/en/): the Swiss software company near Bern that builds ModemLens
